rationale: Both derive every value from the history of guesses rather than mutating counters, which suits the FRP framing. B models this more cleanly. A frozen GameState dataclass holds the immutable snapshot, all derived values (guessed, failures, remaining_guesses, status, masked_word) are properties, and a pure reduce function produces the next state. The Hangman class is a thin wrapper. Each piece has a clear docstring, and the failures calculation is concise. A is simpler and normalises letter case, which B does not. However, it mixes the derived logic into the mutable class and re-scans the guesses in a loop to count failures. The name reduce mildly shadows functools.reduce. Overall B's design is more principled and still easy to read.
